Render runs the application's Docker image on a free web service: it sleeps after 15 minutes without requests (waking up takes about a minute) and has no persistent disk, H2 and the chosen passwords are gone after every restart. Render's free PostgreSQL expires after 30 days: if you did step 11, set engine postgresql in spec/base/architecture.adl back to engine h2. pisa play never plays this step (everything skip).

1. The lines in the .adl. The pipeline block (step 10) gets release github and deploy render; deploy needs the docker block, which you already have (step 2). If you skipped step 10, write the whole block before the last bracket:

    pipeline {
        ci github
        release github
        deploy render
    }

Then apply the .adl again (render.yml and .github/workflows/cd.yml are created, once, after that they are yours):

pisa init --target spring-boot --out . --group ch.example --artifact adressen-spring --adl spec/base/architecture.adl --force

You should see: render.yml and .github/workflows/cd.yml in the list and Deploy to Render: the comments at the top of render.yml say how.

2. Set up at Render (in the browser). Push the project to GitHub (step 10). On dashboard.render.com New ▸ Blueprint, pick the repository and enter render.yml in the field Blueprint Path (Render looks for render.yaml by default). Then in the service Settings ▸ Deploy Hook copy the URL and save it in the GitHub repository under Settings ▸ Secrets and variables ▸ Actions as the secret RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL. The URL is secret: never write it into a file.

3. Deploy. Only the deploy hook deploys, so only a tag v* (the release workflow creates the release, cd.yml calls the hook):

git add -A && git commit -m "Deploy to Render"
git tag v0.1.0
git push origin main v0.1.0

You should see: in the repository under Actions the run Deploy, at Render a new deploy and after a few minutes the application at the address of the service (https://<name>.onrender.com/login.html). The first access after sleeping takes about a minute. More about it: User Guide, section "Deploying to Render". Pisa has not yet checked this on a real Render account: whether 512 MB are enough for Spring and whether the service accepts the healthCheckPath is unchecked.

docs.title: 13. Accept: user stories (optional)
docs.text:
This is an extra as well; pisa play never plays this step (everything skip). So far you checked the generated application with the tests Pisa writes. A user story is the other side: someone who asked for something says when it is done as he asked for it. pisa story works for a story of your application in the same five phases as the specs of Pisa itself (pisa extend), with one folder per story, spec/features/NNN-<feature>/stories/NNN-<story>/ (a feature is a folder with feature.md and its stories, here one feature with one story), and one file per phase: 01-spec.md (the criteria), 02-plan.md, 03-test.md (the frozen acceptance tests), 04-implement.md, 05-check.md. pisa story asks no language model: it creates the files, freezes the tests and runs them.

The acceptance tests of a story run only on demand: mvn test does not compile the folder stories/ (the tests of the stories live there, outside src/ and spec/), mvn test -Pac does (the Maven profile ac adds stories as a test folder and sets PISA_ACCEPTANCE=1; it is part of every generated pom.xml, and a project from an earlier version gets it with pisa init … --force). Maven needs the dependencies as for mvn test.

1. Specify. The story in your words; Pisa creates 01-spec.md with a table of criteria:

cd adressen-spring
pisa story --specify "A clerk can archive a person"

You should see Written: …/spec/features/001-clerk-archive-person/stories/001-clerk-archive-person/01-spec.md (and feature.md next to stories/). Open the file and replace the two example rows by what the clerk expects, in his words (one row per criterion, AC1, AC2, …):

| ID | Criterion |
|---|---|
| AC1 | A clerk sets a person to Archived, and the person is still listed with that status |
| AC2 | A clerk cannot give a person a status that does not exist; the person stays as it was |

2. Plan. One task per criterion, in 02-plan.md:

pisa story --plan

3. Test. One acceptance test per criterion, in stories/001-clerk-archive-person/tests/. The folder does not have to match the Java package, but a test must lie in a package below ch.example.adressen, so that Spring finds the application class. Mark each test with @Acceptance (the annotation that pisa init wrote next to the application class; it skips the test unless PISA_ACCEPTANCE=1) and with the JUnit tag of its criterion, @Tag("AC1"): Pisa runs one criterion by its tag (mvn test -Pac -Dgroups=AC1), the class and method names are free:

// stories/001-clerk-archive-person/tests/ArchivePersonTest.java
package ch.example.adressen.stories;

import static org.springframework.security.test.web.servlet.request.SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors.csrf;
import static org.springframework.security.test.web.servlet.request.SecurityMockMvcRequestPostProcessors.user;
import static org.springframework.security.test.web.servlet.setup.SecurityMockMvcConfigurers.springSecurity;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.get;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.post;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.put;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.status;

import ch.example.adressen.Acceptance;
import ch.example.adressen.repository.PersonRepository;
import com.jayway.jsonpath.JsonPath;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Tag;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.MockMvc;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.setup.MockMvcBuilders;
import org.springframework.web.context.WebApplicationContext;

/** Acceptance tests of the story "A clerk can archive a person"; every test carries the tag of its criterion. */
@SpringBootTest
class ArchivePersonTest {

    private static final String PATH = "/api/persons";

    @Autowired
    private WebApplicationContext context;

    @Autowired
    private PersonRepository repository;

    private MockMvc mockMvc;

    @BeforeEach
    void signIn() {
        mockMvc = MockMvcBuilders.webAppContextSetup(context)
                .apply(springSecurity())
                .defaultRequest(get("/").with(user("tester").roles("FULL")).with(csrf()))
                .build();
    }

    @AfterEach
    void cleanUp() {
        repository.deleteAll();
    }

    private static String person(String status) {
        return "{\"firstName\":\"Anna\",\"lastName\":\"Muster\",\"status\":\"" + status
                + "\",\"address\":{\"street\":\"Bahnhofstrasse 1\",\"zip\":\"8001\",\"city\":\"Zürich\"}}";
    }

    private String createPerson() throws Exception {
        String response = mockMvc.perform(post(PATH).contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON).content(person("ACTIVE")))
                .andExpect(status().isOk())
                .andReturn().getResponse().getContentAsString();
        return String.valueOf((Object) JsonPath.read(response, "$.id"));
    }

    @Acceptance
    @Tag("AC1")
    void aPersonSetToArchivedIsStillListedWithThatStatus() throws Exception {
        String id = createPerson();
        mockMvc.perform(put(PATH + "/" + id).contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON).content(person("ARCHIVED")))
                .andExpect(status().isOk());
        mockMvc.perform(get(PATH))
                .andExpect(status().isOk())
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$[0].status").value("ARCHIVED"));
    }

    @Acceptance
    @Tag("AC2")
    void aStatusThatDoesNotExistIsRefusedAndThePersonStaysAsItWas() throws Exception {
        String id = createPerson();
        mockMvc.perform(put(PATH + "/" + id).contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON).content(person("GONE")))
                .andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
        mockMvc.perform(get(PATH + "/" + id))
                .andExpect(status().isOk())
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.status").value("ACTIVE"));
    }
}

Then freeze them:

pisa story --test

03-test.md now lists the file with its SHA-256 under "Frozen files". From here on the test must not change: if it does, --check reports it (see step 5). A test file that you add later and that the table does not list is added to the table by --check, with a warning. (Pisa's own pisa extend --test has a language model write the tests and requires them to fail first; pisa story --test takes the tests you wrote.)

4. Implement. pisa story --implement writes 04-implement.md with the assignment and the open tasks. Here the application already does what the story asks (the generated API accepts every status of the enumeration and refuses others), so there is nothing left to implement; for a story that needs new behavior this is where you, or your coding assistant, work through the plan until the acceptance tests are green.

pisa story --implement

5. Check. Pisa first compares the frozen files with their recorded SHA-256, then runs the acceptance tests, one criterion at a time (mvn test -Pac -Dgroups=AC1; every run starts Maven, so it takes about half a minute per criterion), and writes 05-check.md:

pisa story --check

You should see a tree with the duration of every criterion (a terminal shows coloured ☑ and ☒ instead of ✅ and ❌):

001/001 | A clerk can archive a person
  ✅ frozen tests unchanged
  acceptance
    ✅ AC1: A clerk sets a person to Archived, and the person is still listed with that status · 26.2 s
    ✅ AC2: A clerk cannot give a person a status that does not exist; the person stays as it was · 26.3 s

The exit code is 0 when every criterion is green and nothing frozen changed, otherwise 1; 05-check.md says Converged only then. If you change a frozen test, the tree says so, even when the tests are green:

001/001 | A clerk can archive a person
  ❌ frozen test changed: stories/001-clerk-archive-person/tests/ArchivePersonTest.java
  acceptance
    ✅ AC1: A clerk sets a person to Archived, and the person is still listed with that status · 26.5 s
    ✅ AC2: A clerk cannot give a person a status that does not exist; the person stays as it was · 25.7 s

A frozen file that is missing is reported the same way (frozen test missing: …), and a 03-test.md without the table "Frozen files" says tests are not frozen yet, run pisa story --test.

6. All stories at a glance. --list shows every story with its state, --check --full runs all of them and ends with a summary:

pisa story --list
pisa story --check --full

| Status | Story   | Title                        |
| ------ | ------- | ---------------------------- |
| ✅      | 001/001 | A clerk can archive a person |

| Story   | Title                        | Result | Criteria |
| ------- | ---------------------------- | ------ | -------- |
| 001/001 | A clerk can archive a person | ✅      | 2/2      |

1 of 1 stories accepted
Acceptance criteria: 2 ✅ green, 0 ❌ red (2 in total)

--feature <NNN> --story <NNN> picks one story (--story alone is enough while the story number is unique); pisa story --specify "…" --feature 1 adds a further story to feature 001; --full and --story cannot be combined.
