docs.title: Not yet possible
docs.text:
So you don't go looking for things that aren't there yet (as of 0.15.0):

Area Not yet possible Data model Lists of parts (oneToMany … composed). Setting the inverse side (mappedBy) of a relationship through the API. Other operations than the four of @operations, rights per field. Database Schema migrations (e.g. Flyway) — Hibernate manages the schema; switching H2 ↔ PostgreSQL goes through the architecture plan. Cleanup Pisa never deletes orphaned files from generate; you remove them yourself. Web pages Sorting, searching, number formatting. Switching the display mode on or off, or describing a separate view form (<entity>.view.md); today only through your own page templates. AI proposals Going from requirements to architecture to model in one step (run the commands one after another). Both proposals read requirements.md, and forms and use cases can be derived without an AI (propose-specs). The proposals are tested automatically only against a fake model; with a real model there was one manual run each. propose-architecture proposing runtime hono or authentication session has never run with a real model. Architecture More than one backend or database, gateways, brokers, hexagonal style, assigning entities to backends. A changed .adl needs init --adl … --force. TypeScript target manyToMany, oneToMany without mappedBy, oneToOne without composed, IDs larger than 32-bit. Login User management in the browser, password reset by email, JWT, Keycloak/OIDC, per-field or per-row permissions, HTTPS, login rate limits. Docker One image per project, only Dockerfile and Compose; no image builds in the CI file, no push to a registry, no multi-architecture images, no health check in the Dockerfile itself, no Testcontainers for TypeScript. Port 8080 and /data are fixed. Deployment Any host besides Render; a database at Render; custom domains; a health check test after the deploy. Not checked on a real account. CI and Git hosting Anything besides GitHub (GitLab, Bitbucket, Codeberg); no command that creates the repository on GitHub. The workflows and templates are checked only as valid YAML, not on a real GitHub run. pisa story --specify doesn't ask the model (you fill in the criteria), and --implement only writes the assignment. --check was run for real against npm (Hono) and Maven (Spring, 2026-11-13). The CI step is not part of the generated ci.yml yet. update-versions Docker image tags and the Node.js version line. Pisa won't fix a template that a new version breaks. Checked by hand with real projects (Hono: all 122 tests; Spring: --check build, then replay matches); that a failing version stays behind is shown only by unit tests. pisa play Manual-edit and browser steps. It checks exit codes, not the "you should see" text; with --llm it has never been run with the tutorials. Tests Tests of layout effects in the browser; tests for composed lists; error cases for relationships (the tests of relations set only one row of the other side). Other targets Quarkus and others. The old prisma-hono-ink target doesn't support composed.

Upgrading from 0.9.1 or earlier: add "bootstrap": "5.3.8" to versions in .pisa/architecture.plan.json, then run pisa init --force (Pisa names the missing key).

Upgrading from 0.12.x: init --force removes the old password file (and reports passwords.yml). Passwords users chose earlier no longer apply.

Upgrading from 0.13.x: nothing to do. New projects put their specs in spec/base/; an existing project with files directly in spec/ is left as it is.

docs.title: Writing your own tutorials for pisa play
docs.text:
A tutorial is a Markdown file. Each ```bash block is a command. An HTML comment directly before a block changes how it's handled (invisible to readers):

Comment Effect on the next block <!-- play: write spec/base/a.md --> Its contents are written to this file <!-- play: write spec/base/a.adl unless-llm --> Same, but only when running without --llm (the shown result of an AI step) <!-- play: llm --> Runs only with --llm <!-- play: tests --> Runs tests (mvn test, npm test); skipped with --fast <!-- play: slow --> Slow step (browser tests, replay); skipped with --fast <!-- play: optional --> Optional step (e.g. the CI at the end); runs, but is skipped with --fast <!-- play: skip --> Not run, only listed as a manual step <!-- play: server /login.html --> Starts the app, waits for this path to respond, then stops it; skipped with --fast

All other blocks (expected files as examples, yaml, json) are plain text. An unknown comment, or a comment without a block after it, is an error with a line number.
